title: Harvesting kale microgreens
subtitle: When and how to cut, rinse, and store kale microgreen cotyledons
excerpt: Kale microgreens are ready to cut when the cotyledons are fully open and deep green, around day 8 to 12 from sowing, slightly later than radish or broccoli. Cut 1 cm above the medium. Kale cotyledons have a slightly heartier texture than broccoli and store well for up to three days.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: The seed leaf — the first leaf or pair of leaves produced by a germinating seed. Kale cotyledons are oval and smooth with a slightly waxy surface, ranging from bright green to blue-green depending on variety. They are harvested as the edible microgreen shoot and have a mild, slightly earthy flavour.

The height at which microgreens are cut above the growing medium. Cutting at 1 cm above the surface leaves the root system in the tray and keeps compost away from the cut stems. Standard for all brassica microgreens.

content.text: Kale microgreens are harvested at the cotyledon stage, like all brassica microgreens. The process is the same as for broccoli; kale just takes a day or two longer, and the cotyledons are slightly heartier.

should be fully open (not cupped or partially folded) and a deep, even green, 4 to 7 cm tall. Kale cotyledons have a slightly more robust texture than broccoli cotyledons and take slightly longer to reach full development. Harvest on day 8 to 12, using the visual cue of fully open, vivid cotyledons rather than the day count.

As with broccoli, once tiny true leaves appear from the centre of the cotyledons, the microgreen is past its peak. The flavour sharpens and the texture becomes less tender. Harvest at the cotyledon stage.
Use clean sharp scissors. Work from one side of the tray to the other, cutting horizontally across the stems in one pass.
: 1 cm above the growing medium. Kale microgreens do not produce a usable second cut; add the tray to compost after harvesting.

Rinse under cold water in a colander. Shake out excess moisture. Kale cotyledons are among the more robust brassica microgreens for storage: refrigerate in a sealed container with a dry kitchen paper lining for up to three days.
Kale microgreens hold well in the fridge for up to three days. Cut them a day ahead and they will still be in good shape at serving.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common harvest-stage problems with kale microgreens.

items.symptom: Cotyledons still cupped and not fully flat after day 10
items.cause: Insufficient light or removed from blackout too early.
items.fix: Give another day in bright light before cutting. Fully closed cotyledons indicate either that the light phase was too short or that light levels were too low.

items.symptom: Uneven cotyledon development: some tall and open, some still short and folded
items.cause: Uneven germination at the sowing stage.
items.fix: Harvest what is ready and check again in 24 hours. Kale's slightly longer and more variable development window means some gaps in timing across the tray are normal.

items.symptom: Yellowing within 24 hours in the refrigerator
items.fix: Use dry kitchen paper lining and replace it if it becomes saturated. Kale cotyledons are more forgiving than broccoli but still yellow if stored wet.
